anchorFact.claim: The atestado médico de incapacidade multiuso is mandatory for people with disability of 60% or more to access social, economic and fiscal benefits including IRS, IUC, travel costs and prosthetics support, is issued following evaluation by a medical board which sets the degree and validity, and under artigo 87 of the CIRS allows a deduction of four times the IAS per taxpayer with disability and 2.5 times the IAS per disabled dependant or ascendant.

briefs.notObvious: One certificate serves every scheme, so the effort of obtaining it once is what unlocks tax, vehicle and health benefits together.

briefs.title: Who can be recognised as a principal informal carer
briefs.userQuestion: Can I be recognised as my relative's carer if I already have a job?
briefs.scenario: A family member providing daily care assumes recognition is automatic, or rules themselves out over the relationship degree.
briefs.audience: family members providing full-time care
briefs.promise: The age band, the cohabitation and no-remuneration conditions, and how wide the family relationship can be.

anchorFact.claim: Recognition as cuidador informal principal requires being between 18 and legal retirement age, accompanying the cared-for person permanently, living in the same house, receiving no remuneration from work or for the care, being a spouse or partner in união de facto or a relative or in-law up to the 4th degree in the direct or collateral line, and having adequate health conditions to provide care.

briefs.notObvious: The fourth degree reaches cousins and great-uncles, far wider than people expect, but the no-remuneration condition rules out anyone keeping a job.

briefs.title: The household income ceiling for the informal carer subsidy
briefs.userQuestion: Does recognised carer status come with money?
briefs.scenario: A recognised carer assumes the status carries an automatic payment, and does not check the separate means test.
briefs.audience: recognised informal carers
briefs.promise: That status and subsidy are separate, the household income ceiling expressed against the IAS, and where to apply.

anchorFact.claim: The subsídio de apoio ao cuidador informal principal is separate from recognition of the status and requires the household's monthly reference income to be below 1.3 times the IAS, published as 698.27 euros, with applications made in Segurança Social Direta under Família by selecting Estatuto do cuidador informal.

briefs.notObvious: Recognition and payment are two different applications, so carers who obtain the status often never claim the subsidy attached to it.

briefs.title: The ages that make a public transport pass free
briefs.userQuestion: Is my child's or my own transport pass free?
briefs.scenario: A family keeps paying for a monthly pass, or a student assumes the free pass ended when they left school.
briefs.audience: students and young people using public transport
briefs.promise: The two age-based free passes and the exact month each one stops, plus the discounts for pensioners and disability.

anchorFact.claim: Under the consolidated Portaria on free youth passes, the sub 18+TP pass is free for children and young people aged 4 to 18 and valid until the last day of the month they turn 19, the sub 23+TP pass covers those over 18 until the last day of the month they turn 24, a 50% discount applies to beneficiaries of the solidarity supplement, social integration income and citizens with incapacity of 60% or more, and a 25% discount applies to pensioners whose monthly pension income is at or below 1.2 times the IAS.

briefs.notObvious: Both passes run to the end of the month of a birthday rather than the birthday itself, and the free pass follows age rather than being a student.

briefs.title: The study grant window, and the late route that still pays
briefs.userQuestion: Have we missed the deadline to apply for a higher education grant?
briefs.scenario: A family enrolling late assumes the grant window has closed and does not apply at all.
briefs.audience: higher education students applying for a grant
briefs.promise: The main application window, the twenty-working-day rule for late enrolment, and the later window that still pays proportionally.

anchorFact.claim: For 2026/2027 the bolsa de estudo application runs from 14 August to 2 October, a student enrolling before 2 October has 20 working days to apply even if that runs past the date, and applications between 3 October and 31 May are still accepted with the grant paid proportionally.

briefs.notObvious: A late application still pays a proportional grant, so giving up after the main deadline forfeits money that was still available.

briefs.title: The past property share that can disqualify you from IMT Jovem
briefs.userQuestion: I once inherited part of a house — does that block the under-35 exemption?
briefs.scenario: A first-time buyer who once held a fraction of a family property assumes they still count as a first-time buyer.
briefs.audience: under-35 buyers with a past property interest
briefs.promise: How any prior share of residential property affects the exemption, the three-year rule that restores it, and what happens when only one of a couple qualifies.

anchorFact.claim: IMT Jovem does not apply where a person already owns any part of residential property however acquired, but where that share was sold and more than three years elapse between the sale and the acquisition of the permanent home the right to exemption returns; where only one member of a couple meets the conditions the exemption applies only to the 50% that person acquires.

briefs.notObvious: An inherited fraction counts as ownership, and the three-year clock runs from the sale, so timing a purchase can restore an exemption people assume is permanently lost.

briefs.title: The state guarantee that covers a young buyer's missing deposit
briefs.userQuestion: Can I buy without a deposit if I am under 35?
briefs.scenario: A young buyer with income but no savings assumes the deposit requirement is absolute and stops looking.
briefs.audience: under-35 buyers without a deposit
briefs.promise: How much of the loan the State guarantees, the purchase price ceiling, the income and ownership conditions, and how long the scheme runs.

anchorFact.claim: The garantia pública gives a personal State guarantee of up to 15% of the initially contracted capital so that borrowers aged 18 to 35 with tax domicile in Portugal can obtain 100% financing, requires income up to the 8th IRS bracket, no property ownership, no prior public guarantee and no debts to Finanças or Segurança Social, applies to transactions up to 450,000 euros, lasts 10 years, and covers credit contracts formalised up to 31 December 2026.

briefs.notObvious: The bank's own risk and effort-rate limits still apply, so the guarantee removes the deposit barrier without removing the affordability test.

briefs.title: The business costs where IVA is never fully deductible
briefs.userQuestion: Can I deduct the IVA on the car, the fuel and the client lunch?
briefs.scenario: A business deducts IVA across all its running costs and faces a correction on exactly the categories the law singles out.
briefs.audience: businesses deducting IVA on running costs
briefs.promise: The categories excluded outright, the partial rate on diesel and LPG, and the narrow case where event meals are partly deductible.

anchorFact.claim: Artigo 21 of the CIVA excludes deduction on acquisition, rental, use, transformation and repair of passenger cars, pleasure boats, helicopters, aircraft and motorcycles; IVA on diesel, LPG, natural gas and biofuels is deductible at 50%, and accommodation, food and drink linked to congresses, fairs, exhibitions and similar events contracted directly with organisers and contributing to taxable operations is deductible at 25%.

briefs.notObvious: Fuel is half deductible and event catering a quarter, so the answer is rarely all or nothing and the partial rates are where corrections come from.

briefs.title: The share capital a single-member company actually needs
briefs.userQuestion: How much money do I need to set up a company in Portugal?
briefs.scenario: Someone postpones incorporating because they assume a substantial minimum capital is required.
briefs.audience: people considering incorporating alone
briefs.promise: The minimum quota value, the freedom to set capital, and the five working days to deposit it.

anchorFact.claim: For a sociedade unipessoal por quotas the share capital is freely set in the company contract except where the law provides otherwise, the quota value may vary but can never be below 1.00 euro, and proof of capital deposit in an account in the company's name can be made within five working days after incorporation.

briefs.notObvious: One euro is a lawful capital and the deposit can follow incorporation, so the money is not a barrier to starting that people assume it is.

briefs.title: The register every new company must file within thirty days
briefs.userQuestion: Is there anything to file after incorporating besides tax registration?
briefs.scenario: A founder completes incorporation, opens activity, and never files the beneficial owner declaration nobody mentioned.
briefs.audience: founders of a newly incorporated entity
briefs.promise: The thirty-day initial deadline, the thirty days after any change, the annual confirmation, and who counts as beneficial owner.

anchorFact.claim: The initial RCBE declaration must be filed within 30 days of the NIF being attributed, any change to declared data must be updated within 30 days, entities must confirm the information annually, and the beneficial owner is the ultimate natural person controlling the entity, identified by criteria such as holding more than 25% of share capital or another member's voting rights.

briefs.notObvious: The annual confirmation is separate from the initial filing, so a company compliant on day one drifts out of compliance without doing anything.

briefs.title: The extra medicine subsidy for pensioners on a low income
briefs.userQuestion: Do pensioners pay less for prescriptions?
briefs.scenario: A pensioner on a small pension pays the standard share, never having been told an income-based uplift exists.
briefs.audience: pensioners paying for prescribed medicines
briefs.promise: The additional percentage added to the standard tiers, the annual income ceiling that gates it, and where fuller regimes exist.

anchorFact.claim: Pensioners whose pension does not exceed the minimum wage receive an additional 15% on medicine comparticipação in tiers B, C and D, and this protection applies only to pensioners whose total annual income does not exceed 14 times the national minimum wage, alongside regimes excecionais that raise the rate or reach 100% for defined pathologies and groups.

briefs.notObvious: The ceiling is expressed as fourteen times the minimum wage annually rather than a monthly pension figure, so pensioners rarely recognise that they qualify.

briefs.title: The days of leave owed for a marriage or a death in the family
briefs.userQuestion: How many days off am I entitled to when a close relative dies?
briefs.scenario: A grieving employee takes what the employer offers, or uses holiday, without knowing the statutory entitlement by relationship.
briefs.audience: employees facing a bereavement or marrying
briefs.promise: The consecutive days for marriage, and the three bereavement bands by closeness of relationship.

anchorFact.claim: Under the Código do Trabalho a worker has 15 consecutive days of justified leave for marriage, and for bereavement up to 20 consecutive days for the death of a spouse not separated, child or stepchild, up to 5 consecutive days for a first-degree relative or in-law in the direct line not covered above, and up to 2 consecutive days for another relative or in-law in the direct line or second degree of the collateral line.

briefs.notObvious: The days are consecutive calendar days including weekends, and the twenty-day band for a child or spouse is far longer than most employers volunteer.

briefs.title: The weekly hours a working student can take without losing pay
briefs.userQuestion: What can I ask my employer for if I am studying while working?
briefs.scenario: An employee studying part-time uses holiday for classes and exams, unaware of a statutory time allowance.
briefs.audience: employees studying alongside work
briefs.promise: The flexible schedule obligation, the weekly hours released when flexibility is impossible, and the exam absences that count as justified.

anchorFact.claim: Employers must draw up specific working schedules for a trabalhador-estudante flexible enough for class attendance, and where a flexible regime is not possible the worker is released for up to 6 hours a week without loss of pay or other benefit if the school timetable requires it; absences strictly needed to travel to and sit assessments are justified.

briefs.notObvious: The six hours are a fallback when flexible scheduling fails, not the default, so the first entitlement to ask for is the adjusted schedule itself.

briefs.title: The asset ceiling and the contract behind the social insertion income
briefs.userQuestion: What disqualifies a household from the social insertion income?
briefs.scenario: A household in severe hardship does not apply, assuming any savings or property rules them out entirely.
briefs.audience: households in severe financial hardship
briefs.promise: The movable asset ceiling expressed against the IAS, the 45-day insertion contract, and how the payment is calculated per household member.

anchorFact.claim: Rendimento Social de Inserção requires movable assets not above 60 times the IAS, published as 30,555.60 euros, registration with the employment centre where unemployed and availability for work or training; a contrato de inserção must be signed within 45 days of the award, the benefit is paid for 12 months and renewable, and the amount is the gap between the household reference value and its income, at 100% of the RSI value for the claimant, 70% per other adult and 50% per minor.

briefs.notObvious: The ceiling is on movable assets rather than all property, and the 45-day insertion contract is a condition of keeping the award rather than a formality.

briefs.title: The energy discount that is applied without you asking
briefs.userQuestion: Do I have to apply for the social energy tariff?
briefs.scenario: A household on a low income never applies, assuming a form is required, and pays full price for years.
briefs.audience: low-income households paying energy bills
briefs.promise: That recognition is automatic through data matching, the contracted power limit, the income route that needs no social benefit, and the window to opt out.

anchorFact.claim: The tarifa social for electricity and natural gas has been assigned by automatic recognition since 1 July 2016, applied by suppliers without any customer request, requiring a domestic supply contract in the person's name for permanent housing with contracted power at or below 6.9 kVA and receipt of a qualifying social benefit, or alternatively a household annual income at or below 6,272.64 euros increased by 50% for each member without income; beneficiaries have 30 days to oppose the automatic assignment.

briefs.notObvious: The income route works without receiving any social benefit at all, and because assignment is automatic the usual failure is a contract in the wrong name rather than a missing application.

briefs.title: An imported car first registered abroad before July 2007 pays less IUC
briefs.userQuestion: Why is the IUC on my imported car higher than on an identical Portuguese one?
briefs.scenario: An owner of a car imported from another EU state pays category B IUC on a vehicle whose original registration predates the category change.
briefs.audience: owners of cars imported from the EU
briefs.promise: The rule that moves such vehicles to the older, cheaper category, and the registration dates that decide it.

anchorFact.claim: Since 1 January 2020 vehicles previously taxed in IUC category B that were registered in Portugal on or after 1 July 2007 but had a first registration in an EU or EEA country before that date are taxed in category A, which generally reduces the tax due.

briefs.notObvious: The category follows the original foreign registration date rather than the Portuguese one, and the correction is not applied automatically to every affected vehicle.

briefs.title: Why the age discount on imported car tax is smaller than expected
briefs.userQuestion: How much does the age of an imported car reduce the vehicle tax?
briefs.scenario: A buyer estimates ISV using the age reduction against the whole tax and is caught out by a much larger bill.
briefs.audience: people importing a used car from the EU
briefs.promise: The two components ISV is built from, and which one the age reduction actually applies to.

anchorFact.claim: ISV on passenger cars is the sum of a cilindrada component and an environmental component from Tabela A, and for vehicles with definitive registrations from other EU Member States the Tabela D age reduction percentages apply only to the cilindrada component, so the CO2 environmental component is taxed in full without any age reduction.

briefs.notObvious: Applying the age discount to the whole tax understates the bill badly, because the environmental half never benefits from it.

briefs.title: The fifteen working days that cut a traffic fine by a fifth
briefs.userQuestion: Is it cheaper to just pay a traffic fine straight away?
briefs.scenario: A driver leaves the notice on the counter for a few weeks, then pays the full amount plus costs.
briefs.audience: drivers who have received a traffic fine notice
briefs.promise: The window for the reduced payment, the reduction it gives, when costs start being added, and the separate window to contest.

anchorFact.claim: Voluntary payment of a road traffic coima must be made within 15 working days of notification of the auto and reduces the amount by 20% of the minimum coima applicable, paying within that window and filing no defence avoids costs, while voluntary payment remains possible after 15 working days until the administrative decision but with costs due.

briefs.notObvious: Paying late is not simply paying the same amount later: the reduction disappears and process costs attach on top.

briefs.title: The two clocks that start when an imported car enters Portugal
briefs.userQuestion: How long do I have to register a car I brought in from another country?
briefs.scenario: An owner drives on foreign plates for months, unaware that two separate deadlines started the day the car arrived.
briefs.audience: people importing a vehicle into Portugal
briefs.promise: The customs declaration deadline, the separate driving and registration window it opens, and the inspection certificate's own validity.

anchorFact.claim: After a vehicle enters Portugal the Declaração Aduaneira de Veículo must be submitted within 20 working days, the vehicle may then be driven for 60 consecutive days on the DAV alone and the registration request must be made within those 60 days, and the model 112 inspection certificate issued by a CITV is valid for 90 working days.

briefs.notObvious: Three different periods run at once in working days and consecutive days, and missing the twenty-day customs step invalidates the sixty-day driving allowance that depends on it.

briefs.title: A NIF costs nothing, and whether you need a representative depends on where you live
briefs.userQuestion: How much does a NIF cost and do I need a fiscal representative to get one?
briefs.scenario: Someone abroad pays an agency for a NIF, believing both the number and a representative are unavoidable costs.
briefs.audience: non-residents applying for a Portuguese NIF
briefs.promise: That the request is free, when a representative is genuinely required, and which residents can use the online counter.

anchorFact.claim: Requesting a NIF is free; non-residents in Portugal need an identification document or passport and a fiscal representative resident in national territory, and the e-balcão route on the Portal das Finanças is available to people residing outside the European Union, Norway, Iceland and Liechtenstein.

briefs.notObvious: The representative requirement tracks residence outside the EU/EEA rather than nationality, so many people pay for one they do not need.

briefs.title: Four ways back into Portal das Finanças, only one of which waits for post
briefs.userQuestion: What is the fastest way to recover my Finanças password?
briefs.scenario: Someone locked out requests a password by post and waits days, without checking the instant routes available to them.
briefs.audience: people locked out of Portal das Finanças
briefs.promise: The postal timeline, and the three immediate alternatives including the SMS code and its five-minute window.

anchorFact.claim: Requesting a new Portal das Finanças senha de acesso cancels the previous one and posts a new password to the tax address in an average of 5 business days, while recovery is also possible through the security question, the Cartão de Cidadão or Chave Móvel Digital at Autenticação.gov, or by SMS code to a confirmed phone number which must be entered within 5 minutes.

briefs.notObvious: Requesting the postal password cancels the old one immediately, so choosing that route locks you out for the days it takes to arrive.

briefs.title: Both parents must report joint custody, or the tax benefit collapses to one household
briefs.userQuestion: Do separated parents each have to report the children to Finanças?
briefs.scenario: One parent reports the household by February and assumes that covers both, or the two reports disagree.
briefs.audience: separated parents sharing custody
briefs.promise: The February deadline, what each parent must declare, and exactly what happens when the reports conflict or are missing.

anchorFact.claim: Household composition must be confirmed in the Portal das Finanças by the end of February with reference to 31 December, and for a dependant in guarda conjunta both guardians must report the dependant's tax number and the joint custody; where the annual communication is missing or the guardians' communications are inconsistent, the tax authority treats the dependant as not having alternating residence and the income and the per-dependant deduction fall to the single household that includes them.

briefs.notObvious: Disagreement between the parents is treated the same as silence, so one late or inconsistent filing moves the whole deduction to the other household.

briefs.title: Being IVA exempt does not exempt you from invoicing
briefs.userQuestion: If I am under the Artigo 53 exemption, do I still issue invoices?
briefs.scenario: A newly exempt freelancer issues informal receipts, or omits the required wording, and the invoices are defective.
briefs.audience: freelancers exempt under Artigo 53
briefs.promise: The invoicing obligation that survives the exemption, the exact legend invoices must carry, and the return you are excused from.

anchorFact.claim: Taxpayers exempt under artigo 53 of the CIVA remain subject to the invoicing obligation and their invoices must always carry the mention 'IVA – Regime de Isenção', while they are exempt from submitting the declaração recapitulativa and do not declare operations for IVA purposes.

briefs.notObvious: The exemption removes the tax and most returns but not the paperwork, and a missing legend is what makes an otherwise valid invoice defective.

briefs.title: The retirement savings deduction shrinks as you get older
briefs.userQuestion: How much do I get back on IRS for paying into a PPR?
briefs.scenario: Someone starts a retirement plan late assuming the tax relief is the same at any age, and over-contributes for the benefit available.
briefs.audience: people paying into a retirement savings plan
briefs.promise: The percentage deducted, and the three age bands that cap it.

anchorFact.claim: Under artigo 21 of the EBF, PPR contributions are deductible from IRS tax at 20% of amounts paid in the year, capped at 400 euros per taxpayer under 35, 350 euros between 35 and 50, and 300 euros above 50.

briefs.notObvious: The cap falls with age, so the amount worth contributing purely for the deduction is highest for the youngest savers.

briefs.title: When you can take money out of a PPR without losing the tax benefit
briefs.userQuestion: Can I access my retirement savings early without a penalty?
briefs.scenario: Someone facing unemployment or a large education cost leaves the money untouched, assuming any early withdrawal is penalised.
briefs.audience: PPR holders needing access to funds
briefs.promise: The circumstances allowing penalty-free withdrawal, the age that opens it more broadly, and what a non-qualifying withdrawal costs.

anchorFact.claim: A PPR can be redeemed in whole or part without penalty in cases of pre-retirement, early retirement, old-age or invalidity retirement, death of the participant, long-term unemployment, serious illness or permanent incapacity for work, and from age 60, or where the participant or a household member attends professional or higher education with expenses that year; redemption outside these conditions requires returning the tax benefits obtained plus an additional penalty.

briefs.notObvious: Long-term unemployment and a household member's tuition both qualify, which are exactly the moments people assume the money is locked away.

briefs.title: How many instalments a tax debt can be split into
briefs.userQuestion: Can I spread a tax bill I cannot pay in one go?
briefs.scenario: Someone facing an unaffordable assessment ignores it rather than asking, and the debt moves to enforcement.
briefs.audience: taxpayers facing an unaffordable assessment
briefs.promise: The usual instalment ceiling and minimum amount, the exceptional longer plan, and the missed payments that cancel it.

anchorFact.claim: Instalment payment requires a demonstrated economic situation preventing regularisation within legal deadlines and no other debts to the Autoridade Tributária; the number of instalments is generally up to 36, each at least 1 unidade de conta, extendable to 5 years where the debt exceeds 500 UC with each instalment at least 10 UC, juros de mora accrue on each instalment, and failure to pay 3 successive or 6 interpolated instalments makes the remainder fall due.

briefs.notObvious: The plan survives an occasional missed payment but not three in a row, and the interest keeps running on the outstanding balance throughout.

briefs.title: The two routes to contest a tax assessment, and their clocks
briefs.userQuestion: My IRS assessment looks wrong — how do I challenge it and by when?
briefs.scenario: Someone disputes an assessment by phone or email, and the real deadlines pass while they wait for someone to fix it.
briefs.audience: taxpayers disputing an assessment
briefs.promise: The administrative complaint window, the shorter window after it is rejected, and when interest is owed back to you.

anchorFact.claim: Under artigo 70 of the CPPT a reclamação graciosa may be filed on the same grounds as judicial challenge within 120 days of the facts in artigo 102, and on express or tacit rejection the taxpayer may bring an impugnação judicial within 30 days of the rejection notification or of the presumption of tacit rejection; indemnity interest is due where error attributable to the tax services caused an overpayment.

briefs.notObvious: Silence counts as rejection and starts the thirty-day court clock, so waiting for a reply is itself how the second deadline is missed.

briefs.title: Settling a Social Security debt online, and the limits that allow it
briefs.userQuestion: Can I arrange a Social Security debt plan without going to a counter?
briefs.scenario: Someone with arrears assumes any plan means an appointment and enforcement, and does nothing.
briefs.audience: people with Social Security arrears
briefs.promise: The debt ceilings that keep the request online, the instalment counts by debt size, and how far back arrears are visible.

anchorFact.claim: An instalment request is made in Segurança Social Direta where total debt in enforcement is below 100,000 euros, with debt below 5,000 euros per process for individuals and 10,000 euros for legal persons; instalments run to 36 where the debt is below 3,060 euros, 60 where it exceeds that, and up to 150 under conditions including demonstrated notable financial difficulty, and both employers and independent workers can view amounts owed from the last five years.

briefs.notObvious: The whole arrangement can be made online below the thresholds, which is the step people skip because they expect a counter and an enforcement officer.

briefs.title: The contributory status declaration expires in four months
briefs.userQuestion: How long is my Social Security clearance certificate valid for?
briefs.scenario: Someone obtains the declaration early for a tender, licence or grant and finds it expired when it is finally needed.
briefs.audience: people submitting a contributory clearance certificate
briefs.promise: What the declaration proves and exactly how long it remains valid.

anchorFact.claim: The declaração da situação contributiva proves whether a person's situation with Segurança Social is regularised or in debt, and the declaration is valid for 4 months.

briefs.notObvious: Four months is short enough that obtaining it at the start of an application often means obtaining it twice.

briefs.title: Neighbour noise between 23:00 and 07:00 can be stopped on the spot
briefs.userQuestion: Can the police actually do anything about a noisy neighbour at night?
briefs.scenario: Someone kept awake by a party assumes police will not intervene in a private dispute and endures it.
briefs.audience: people disturbed by neighbour noise
briefs.promise: The night-time window in which noise can be halted immediately, and the written route for anything outside it.

anchorFact.claim: Under the Regulamento Geral do Ruído, neighbourhood noise is not subject to the legally established acoustic requirements, but where it occurs between 23:00 and 07:00 it can be stopped immediately at the request of the disturbed party through intervention by any police authority; outside that window a written complaint goes to the licensing or supervising entity, or through the iFAMA platform.

briefs.notObvious: Neighbour noise sits outside the technical noise limits entirely, so the night-time immediate-halt power is the only fast remedy and it is time-bounded.

briefs.title: Four months to microchip and register a new pet
briefs.userQuestion: By when must I register a puppy or kitten?
briefs.scenario: A new owner waits until the first vaccination appointment or the animal is fully grown, past the registration deadline.
briefs.audience: owners of a new dog, cat or ferret
briefs.promise: The deadline from birth, who may implant the chip, and the separate parish licence that is easy to forget.

anchorFact.claim: All dogs, cats and ferrets must be marked with a transponder and registered in the SIAC, animals born after 25 October 2019 must be marked and registered within 120 days of birth, identification may only be performed by a veterinarian, and failure to register the transponder or the mandatory prophylaxis is a contraordenação.

briefs.notObvious: The clock runs from the animal's birth rather than from when you acquired it, so a pet adopted at three months leaves very little time.

briefs.title: Registering the microchip does not licence the dog
briefs.userQuestion: Is the SIAC registration the same as licensing my dog?
briefs.scenario: An owner completes the microchip registration and assumes all legal obligations are met, until a licence check.
briefs.audience: dog owners who have completed SIAC registration
briefs.promise: The second obligation at the parish council, and the penalty for skipping it.

anchorFact.claim: Beyond SIAC registration, dogs are subject to licenciamento at the junta de freguesia, and failure to comply with the licensing obligation constitutes a contraordenação.

briefs.notObvious: Two separate registers with two separate authorities, and completing the national one gives no notice that the parish one is outstanding.

briefs.title: Which foreign residents can vote in Portuguese local elections
briefs.userQuestion: Can I vote in local elections as a foreign resident?
briefs.scenario: A long-term foreign resident assumes voting is only for citizens and never registers.
briefs.audience: foreign residents in Portugal
briefs.promise: The nationalities that qualify, the residence periods some require, where to register, and the cut-off before an election.

anchorFact.claim: Local election voting is open to Portuguese citizens, Brazilian citizens with equal political rights status, EU nationals aged 17 or over registered in Portugal, and nationals of Brazil without that status, Cape Verde, Argentina, Chile, Colombia, Iceland, Norway, New Zealand, Peru, the United Kingdom, Uruguay or Venezuela resident in Portugal for more than two or three years depending on the country; recenseamento eleitoral registration is at the junta de freguesia of the address on the residence title, and recenseamento is suspended from the 60th day before an election.

briefs.notObvious: There is no general registration deadline, only a sixty-day cut-off before each election, so registering the month before is already too late.

briefs.title: Free dental care during pregnancy, and the window after the birth
briefs.userQuestion: Is dental treatment free while I am pregnant?
briefs.scenario: An expectant parent postpones dental treatment on cost grounds, unaware the SNS covers it and that the entitlement expires after the birth.
briefs.audience: pregnant patients followed by the SNS
briefs.promise: How many vouchers pregnancy entitles you to, who hands them over, and the deadline for using them after the birth.

anchorFact.claim: A pregnant patient followed in SNS services is entitled to a maximum of 3 cheques-dentista, handed over by the family doctor, usable until 60 days after the date of birth, with the treatments free of charge.

briefs.notObvious: The vouchers expire sixty days after the birth, which is exactly the period when a new parent is least likely to book a dentist.

briefs.title: The other groups the dentist voucher covers
briefs.userQuestion: Can adults get free dental care on the SNS?
briefs.scenario: Someone assumes dental care is entirely private in Portugal and never asks whether they fall into a covered group.
briefs.audience: SNS users wondering about dental cover
briefs.promise: The pensioner route through the solidarity supplement, and the specific childhood ages the school programme covers.

anchorFact.claim: The cheque-dentista gives free access to oral health care to SNS users who are beneficiaries of the Complemento Solidário para Idosos, and the Programa Nacional de Promoção de Saúde Oral covers children and young people at ages 7, 10 and 13 and those with special health needs.

briefs.notObvious: Eligibility runs through another benefit rather than age alone, so pensioners who never claimed the solidarity supplement also lose the dental cover attached to it.

briefs.title: The fifty-euro cap on losses from an unauthorised payment
briefs.userQuestion: If money leaves my account fraudulently, who bears the loss?
briefs.scenario: A victim of card or homebanking fraud assumes the money is gone and negotiates with the bank from a position of ignorance.
briefs.audience: victims of unauthorised bank transactions
briefs.promise: The liability cap, the refund deadline the bank must meet, what removes the cap, and the effect of alerting the bank.

anchorFact.claim: For an unauthorised payment operation the customer may bear at most 50 euros, and the provider must reimburse by the end of the first business day following notification except where there is suspicion of fraud by the customer; the cap does not apply where the customer failed to comply with security rules, and after alerting the bank to loss, theft or misappropriation of card or homebanking credentials the customer cannot be charged for later unauthorised movements.

briefs.notObvious: Notification is what stops the clock and shifts the loss, so the minutes spent deciding whether to call the bank are the expensive part.

briefs.title: The income floor below which IRS is not payable
briefs.userQuestion: Do I pay IRS if I earn the minimum wage?
briefs.scenario: A low earner assumes tax is owed on every euro and does not understand why their assessment comes back at zero, or expects a refund that never applies.
briefs.audience: people on low incomes filing IRS
briefs.promise: How the reference value is calculated, and the purpose it serves for minimum-wage earners.

anchorFact.claim: Under artigo 70 of the CIRS the reference value of the mínimo de existência equals the greater of 12,880 euros and 1.5 × 14 × the IAS, and its uprating is intended to keep those earning the national minimum wage exempt from IRS.

briefs.notObvious: It is defined as the higher of a fixed figure and an IAS formula, so it moves each year and the exemption follows the minimum wage rather than a fixed salary.

briefs.title: Nationality through marriage, and the extra step unmarried couples need
briefs.userQuestion: Can I get nationality through my Portuguese partner if we never married?
briefs.scenario: A couple in a long unmarried relationship applies like a married couple and the request stalls for want of a court decision.
briefs.audience: foreign partners of Portuguese nationals
briefs.promise: The three-year requirement for both routes, the judicial recognition unmarried couples must obtain first, and the fee.

anchorFact.claim: Under artigo 3 of the Lei da Nacionalidade (Lei 37/81) a foreigner married for more than three years to a Portuguese national may declare for nationality, while an unmarried partner living in união de facto for more than three years must first obtain judicial recognition of that union and provide a declaration by the Portuguese national made less than three months earlier confirming it continues; the fee is 250 euros to the Conservatória dos Registos Centrais.

briefs.notObvious: The unmarried route needs a court judgment before the application even starts, which adds a separate proceeding most couples do not anticipate.

briefs.title: Legal aid covers the lawyer, not just the court fees
briefs.userQuestion: Can I get help paying for a lawyer if I cannot afford one?
briefs.scenario: Someone with a genuine legal problem does nothing because they price a lawyer before checking whether the State would appoint one.
briefs.audience: people who cannot afford legal costs
briefs.promise: What legal aid actually covers, where the means test is decided, the decision deadline, and the ten days you get to respond to a refusal.

anchorFact.claim: Apoio judiciário includes appointment of a lawyer and payment of their fees or those of the defensor oficioso, exemption from court costs and assignment of an enforcement agent; economic insufficiency is assessed on household income, assets and permanent expenses by Segurança Social, which answers within 30 days and must give written notice with 10 days to respond before a refusal becomes final.

briefs.notObvious: The scheme pays the lawyer as well as waiving the fees, and a refusal is not final until a ten-day reply window has passed.

briefs.title: The small-claims court that costs 35 euros to start
briefs.userQuestion: Is there a cheaper alternative to court for a small dispute?
briefs.scenario: Someone owed a modest sum writes it off, assuming any legal action costs more than the claim is worth.
briefs.audience: people with a low-value civil dispute
briefs.promise: The value ceiling and subjects covered, the fees for winning, losing and settling, and how long it takes.

anchorFact.claim: Julgados de paz resolve civil disputes up to 15,000 euros excluding family matters and debts under adhesion contracts, each party pays an initial 35 euros, the process costs nothing for the winning party and 70 euros for the losing one, mediation settlement costs 50 euros in total, cases take around two and a half months, and appeal is possible where the value exceeds 2,500 euros.

briefs.notObvious: Winning costs nothing beyond the initial 35 euros, which changes the arithmetic on claims people currently abandon.

briefs.title: Consumer arbitration is free in most centres
briefs.userQuestion: What does it cost to take a consumer dispute to arbitration?
briefs.scenario: A consumer with an unresolved complaint assumes arbitration means legal costs and drops the matter.
briefs.audience: consumers with an unresolved dispute
briefs.promise: How many centres exist, how few charge, the dispute value they handle, and the three mechanisms available.

anchorFact.claim: Portugal has 12 authorised consumer conflict arbitration centres resolving disputes through mediation, conciliation or arbitration, the process is free or low cost with only 4 centres charging fees, centres supported by the Ministério da Justiça are typically free, and they handle consumer disputes up to 5,000 euros.

briefs.notObvious: Only a third of the centres charge anything, so the assumed cost barrier usually does not exist for the centre covering your area.

briefs.title: A criminal record certificate is valid for ninety days and names its purpose
briefs.userQuestion: How long does a criminal record certificate last and what does it cost?
briefs.scenario: Someone obtains a certificate early for an application and finds it expired, or that it names the wrong purpose.
briefs.audience: people asked for a criminal record certificate
briefs.promise: The validity period, the fee, that it is requested online, and the purpose declaration it must carry.

anchorFact.claim: A certificado de registo criminal is valid for 90 days from issue, each request costs 5 euros paid by Multibanco with defined free purposes, it can be requested and obtained entirely online, and the concrete and precise purpose for which it is intended must be stated.

briefs.notObvious: The stated purpose is part of the certificate, so one obtained for a different reason may be rejected even while still inside its ninety days.

briefs.title: The property value where a second annual tax starts
briefs.userQuestion: At what property value does the extra IMI surcharge begin?
briefs.scenario: An owner holding two or three properties assumes the annual bill is IMI alone and is surprised by a second assessment in September.
briefs.audience: people owning Portuguese property
briefs.promise: The deduction that shields most owners, the three rate bands above it, and the June assessment that produces a September bill.

anchorFact.claim: AIMI deducts 600,000 euros from the taxable value for an individual taxpayer or undivided inheritance, then charges 0.7 per cent up to 1,000,000 euros, 1 per cent on the excess from 1,000,000 to 2,000,000 euros and 1.5 per cent above 2,000,000 euros, and is assessed by the AT during June with notification to pay in a single instalment in September.

briefs.notObvious: The deduction applies to the combined value of everything you own, not to each property, so three modest homes can cross a line one home never would.

briefs.title: Married owners can double the AIMI deduction by opting in
briefs.userQuestion: Does being married change what we pay on the IMI surcharge?
briefs.scenario: A couple is assessed individually on separately registered properties and pays a surcharge that joint taxation would have removed.
briefs.audience: married and de facto couples owning property
briefs.promise: What the joint option changes, the deduction it unlocks, and the effect on the rate bands.

anchorFact.claim: Where married taxpayers or those in a união de facto opt for joint AIMI taxation the deduction rises from 600,000 euros to 1,200,000 euros and the band values double while the rates stay unchanged.

briefs.notObvious: It is an option that has to be exercised, not an automatic consequence of being married, and the bands double as well as the deduction.

briefs.title: Eight days to answer when your landlord sells
briefs.userQuestion: Do I get first refusal if the flat I rent is put up for sale?
briefs.scenario: A tenant receives a formal notice of a sale project, treats it as information rather than an offer, and loses the right by saying nothing.
briefs.audience: long-term tenants
briefs.promise: How long the tenancy must have run, what the landlord must send, and the short window before the right lapses.

anchorFact.claim: Under artigo 1091.º of the Código Civil the tenant holds a direito de preferência on the sale or dação em cumprimento of premises rented for more than three years, and the party bound to give preference must communicate the sale project and the contract clauses so the right can be exercised within eight days, sob pena de caducidade, unless a shorter period binds them or a longer one is granted.

briefs.notObvious: Silence is not neutral: the eight days run from the communication and the right expires when they pass.

briefs.title: The twelve exempt months that do not count towards a pension
briefs.userQuestion: Should I start paying Segurança Social before my first year is up?
briefs.scenario: A new freelancer enjoys a year of no contributions and later finds that year missing from their contribution record and from any benefit entitlement.
briefs.audience: newly registered independent workers
briefs.promise: What the first-year exemption costs you, how to waive it, and the declaration through which the request is made.

anchorFact.claim: Contributions are not compulsory for people who opened independent activity less than 12 months ago, the worker may instead decline the exemption or ask to be brought into the Regime dos Trabalhadores Independentes early through the declaração trimestral, and if they do not contribute those 12 months will not count towards retirement.

briefs.notObvious: The exemption is a default you can turn down, and turning it down is what buys the year of pension record and benefit eligibility.

briefs.title: Having Chave Móvel Digital does not mean you can sign yet
briefs.userQuestion: Why can I log in with CMD but not sign a document?
briefs.scenario: Someone with a working CMD login reaches a form that requires a signature and discovers at the deadline that signing was never switched on.
briefs.audience: people using CMD for official services
briefs.promise: That signing is a separate activation, who can activate it, and that it can be done at any time after the CMD itself.

anchorFact.claim: The digital signature of the Chave Móvel Digital is activated separately from the CMD: anyone over 16 who holds a Chave Móvel Digital can activate it, either at the moment the CMD is activated or on a later date.

briefs.notObvious: Authentication and signature are two different capabilities behind the same credential, so a working login proves nothing about being able to sign.

briefs.title: The fifty-thousand line that turns a quarterly return monthly
briefs.userQuestion: Do I file the recapitulative statement monthly or quarterly?
briefs.scenario: A trader files quarterly out of habit, crosses the goods threshold in one strong quarter, and is late on every month after it.
briefs.audience: traders selling into the EU
briefs.promise: The two filing rhythms, the amount that switches you between them, and the lookback that keeps you there.

anchorFact.claim: For taxpayers in the normal IVA regime the declaração recapitulativa is due by the 20th of the month following the operations where intra-community transmissions of goods exceed 50,000 euros in the current quarter or in any of the 4 preceding quarters, and otherwise by the 20th of the month following the end of the calendar quarter.

briefs.notObvious: The four-quarter lookback means one big quarter keeps you on monthly filing for a year after the sales stop.

briefs.title: The drinks that leave a restaurant bill at the top rate
briefs.userQuestion: Does the whole restaurant bill get the intermediate IVA rate?
briefs.scenario: A café applies one rate to the whole ticket and under-charges IVA on every soft drink and beer it sells.
briefs.audience: people running food and drink businesses
briefs.promise: Which part of a food and drink service takes the intermediate rate, and the four drink categories carved out of it.

anchorFact.claim: Verba 3.1 of Lista II of the Código do IVA applies the intermediate rate to food and beverage services with the exception of alcoholic drinks, refrigerantes, sumos, néctares and carbonated waters, which fall outside it.

briefs.notObvious: The carve-out is by drink category rather than by whether it is served, so a still juice and a sparkling water can be taxed differently on the same tray.

briefs.title: Time abroad that still counts towards permanent residence
briefs.userQuestion: Does leaving Portugal for a while reset my five years?
briefs.scenario: An EU citizen who spent months abroad for work or a serious illness assumes the clock restarted and delays applying for years.
briefs.audience: EU citizens approaching five years in Portugal
briefs.promise: When the permanent residence certificate becomes available, and the two absence allowances that do not interrupt the count.

anchorFact.claim: The certificado de residência permanente can only be requested by EU nationals and their family members after 5 years of legal residence, and in counting those years temporary absences of up to 6 consecutive months per year do not count, nor do absences of up to 12 consecutive months for justified reasons such as pregnancy or childbirth, serious illness, studies or professional training, or a work posting to another country.

briefs.notObvious: The longer twelve-month allowance is tied to named reasons, so the same absence can either count or not depending on why it happened.

briefs.title: The student earnings that do not count against a grant
briefs.userQuestion: Will my part-time job cost me my study grant?
briefs.scenario: A student turns down work, or hides it, believing any earnings will push the household over the per-capita income limit.
briefs.audience: students working while studying
briefs.promise: How the household per-capita income is tested and the slice of a working student's own pay that is left out of it.

anchorFact.claim: Under the Regulamento das Bolsas de Estudo no âmbito da Ação Social no Ensino Superior, the income of trabalhadores-estudantes up to 14 times the retribuição mínima mensal garantida is exempt for the purposes of calculating rendimento per capita in a grant application.

briefs.notObvious: The exemption is expressed as a multiple of the minimum wage rather than a fixed sum, so it rises every year the minimum wage does.

briefs.title: When a private nursery place becomes free too
briefs.userQuestion: Our solidarity network has no places. Do we have to pay privately?
briefs.scenario: A family told there are no free places gives up and pays a private fee that the State would have covered.
briefs.audience: parents looking for a creche place
briefs.promise: The order in which the free network is used up, and the adhering private creches that free places extend to.

anchorFact.claim: Children born from 1 September 2021 enrolled in creches of the rede solidária, the rede pública, amas da Segurança Social or in for-profit private creches belonging to the bolsa de creches aderentes are entitled to a free place, and the extension of gratuitidade to adhering creches is activated when the offer of the rede solidária with a cooperation agreement or of the SCML is exhausted.

briefs.notObvious: The private route is not a fallback you apply for separately; it opens only once the solidarity network is full, which is exactly when families stop asking.

briefs.title: A bank that turns down a basic account owes you the reason in writing
briefs.userQuestion: The branch said no to a conta de serviços mínimos. Is that the end of it?
briefs.scenario: Someone is told at the counter that the account is not available to them, accepts it, and keeps paying full maintenance fees.
briefs.audience: people refused a basic bank account
briefs.promise: The single lawful ground for refusal, the written notice the bank owes you, and where the notice must point you next.

anchorFact.claim: A credit institution may only refuse a conta de serviços mínimos bancários where the person holds more than one current account deposit, and it must inform the customer of the refusal immediately and free of charge on paper or another durable medium, stating the grounds and the mechanisms available if the customer disagrees, including a complaint to Banco de Portugal and alternative dispute resolution.

briefs.notObvious: A verbal no at the counter is not a refusal in the legal sense, and asking for it in writing is what produces either the account or an appealable decision.

briefs.title: Holding other accounts and still joining a basic one
briefs.userQuestion: Can I open a low-cost account with my parent if I already have my own?
briefs.scenario: An adult child helping an older parent is told the account is unavailable because the child already banks elsewhere.
briefs.audience: families supporting an older or disabled relative
briefs.promise: The general one-account rule and the two circumstances that let someone with other accounts join as co-holder.

anchorFact.claim: A conta de serviços mínimos bancários may only be held by someone who holds no other current account, but a person holding other current accounts may be co-holder together with a person over 65 years of age, or with a duly certified permanent disability of 60 per cent or more, who has no other accounts.

briefs.notObvious: The exception is written around the older or disabled holder, so it survives the helper having a full bank relationship of their own.

briefs.title: Twelve points to start, and the two ways to get above it
briefs.userQuestion: How does the Portuguese driving licence points system actually work?
briefs.scenario: A driver treats the points balance as a one-way count towards losing the licence and never learns it can rise.
briefs.audience: holders of a Portuguese driving licence
briefs.promise: The starting balance, what serious and very serious offences cost, and the two routes that add points back.

anchorFact.claim: Every driver starts with 12 points under the carta por pontos system in force since 1 June 2016; contraordenações graves can subtract 3 points and muito graves 5 points; a driver gains 3 points for each 3-year period without serious or very serious offences or road crimes up to a maximum of 15, and 1 point at each licence revalidation where they voluntarily attend road safety training, up to a maximum of 16.

briefs.notObvious: The ceiling is not twelve. Three clean years and a voluntary course put a driver above the starting balance, which is the buffer nobody builds.

briefs.title: The points course that is not optional once you are low
briefs.userQuestion: What happens when my licence points drop that low?
briefs.scenario: A driver summoned to road safety training does not attend, treating it as advisory, and loses the licence outright.
briefs.audience: drivers who have lost points
briefs.promise: The point level that triggers compulsory training, and what an unjustified absence costs.

anchorFact.claim: A driver on 5 or 4 points under the carta por pontos system must attend a road safety training action, and an unjustified failure to attend implies cassação of the driving title, meaning the driver loses the licence and must wait 2 years before taking it again.

briefs.notObvious: Losing the licence here is not a penalty for the driving. It is a penalty for missing the appointment.

briefs.title: Two years at the same address in the AT records is the proof
briefs.userQuestion: What do we need to prove we live in união de facto for IRS?
briefs.scenario: An unmarried couple assembles parish declarations and certified documents that the Tax Authority did not need from them.
briefs.audience: unmarried couples filing IRS
briefs.promise: When no proof at all is required, and the exact bundle needed when the address route does not work.

anchorFact.claim: Where both taxpayers are resident in Portuguese territory and registered with the Autoridade Tributária at the same tax address for 2 years and during the tax period, no proof of the união de facto is required; where the same tax domicile cannot be verified, the minimum two-year period may be proved by any legally admissible means, and proof through a declaration issued by the competent junta de freguesia must be accompanied by a sworn declaration from the taxpayers and certified copies of each person's birth registration.

briefs.notObvious: Keeping the tax address updated is itself the evidence, which is why couples who never moved it need nothing further.

briefs.title: Filing together or apart when you are not married
briefs.userQuestion: Should we file one IRS return or two?
briefs.scenario: An unmarried couple files separately by default and never checks whether one joint return would have taxed them less.
briefs.audience: unmarried couples with or without children
briefs.promise: The two filing options open to a de facto couple, who must sign what, and how dependants are split under each.

anchorFact.claim: A couple in união de facto, with or without children, may opt for tributação conjunta of their income by submitting a single return authenticated by both, or each may submit their own return under separate taxation, in which case 50 per cent of dependants' income is included in each declaration.

briefs.notObvious: It is a yearly choice rather than a status, and the joint return only counts if both authenticate it.

briefs.title: The water discount your council has to have adopted first
briefs.userQuestion: Why does the water social tariff work for a friend but not for me?
briefs.scenario: Someone already receiving the automatic energy discount assumes water works the same way and never asks their supplier.
briefs.audience: households receiving social supports
briefs.promise: Which supports trigger the water social tariff, the household income route, and the municipal step that decides whether it exists where you live.

anchorFact.claim: The water tarifa social is granted automatically to people receiving supports including the complemento solidário para idosos, rendimento social de inserção, subsídio social de desemprego, abono de família, pensão social de invalidez or pensão social de velhice, or whose household has annual income of 5,808 euros or less increased by 50 per cent for each household member, but adherence to this automatic regime is voluntary and depends on a deliberation of the assembleia municipal on a proposal from the câmara municipal.

briefs.notObvious: Energy is national and automatic; water is decided council by council, so the same household qualifies in one municipality and not the next.

briefs.title: Two cubic metres more per person past four
briefs.userQuestion: Our water bill jumps because we are a big household. Is there anything for that?
briefs.scenario: A household of six is pushed into expensive consumption bands by size alone and pays a premium the tariff rules were written to remove.
briefs.audience: households of five or more people
briefs.promise: The large-family water tariff, how much the cheapest band widens per person, and the registration detail that qualifies you.

anchorFact.claim: ERSAR's commercial relations regulation obliges entidades gestoras to implement tarifários for famílias numerosas wherever the variable tariff is set by escalões, consisting of widening the first escalão by 2 cubic metres for each member of the household beyond 4, with all residents having their tax domicile at the dwelling served.

briefs.notObvious: The qualifying test is where everyone's tax address is registered, so a household member who never updated theirs quietly shrinks the allowance.

briefs.title: The unemployment benefit that exists for one-client freelancers
briefs.userQuestion: If my only client drops me, is there anything like unemployment benefit?
briefs.scenario: A freelancer whose sole contracting entity ends the arrangement assumes independent workers have no unemployment cover and never applies.
briefs.audience: freelancers working mainly for one client
briefs.promise: Who the subsídio por cessação de atividade is for, the contribution record it needs, and the two moments economic dependence is tested at.

anchorFact.claim: The subsídio por cessação de atividade is paid to independent workers economically dependent on a single entidade contratante and requires cumulatively an involuntary end to the contract, 360 days of economically dependent independent activity with contributions actually paid in the 24 months immediately before the cessation, economic dependence both in the previous civil year and at the date of cessation, and registration at the centro de emprego for the area of residence.

briefs.notObvious: Dependence is tested twice, at two different dates, so a freelancer who diversified in the final months can fall out of cover exactly when they lose the client.

briefs.title: Three days or ten before sick pay starts
briefs.userQuestion: When does sick pay actually start after I stop working?
briefs.scenario: A freelancer budgets for a short unpaid gap the way an employee would and is a week out on the arithmetic.
briefs.audience: workers taking sick leave
briefs.promise: The two waiting periods, which status each applies to, and the day payment begins for an independent worker.

anchorFact.claim: The período de espera for subsídio de doença is 3 days for employees and 10 days for independent workers, so an independent worker's subsidy begins on the 11th day of incapacity for work.

briefs.notObvious: A freelancer carries more than three times the unpaid gap an employee does for the same illness, which is what makes a short illness expensive rather than inconvenient.

briefs.title: Where a freelancer's accident insurance stops covering them
briefs.userQuestion: Does my work accident insurance follow me when I work abroad?
briefs.scenario: A freelancer takes a month-long assignment in another EU country and is uninsured for most of it without knowing.
briefs.audience: freelancers who work outside Portugal
briefs.promise: The territory the standard policy covers, the day count that ends it, and when an extension has to be contracted.

anchorFact.claim: An independent worker's seguro de acidentes de trabalho is valid throughout Portuguese territory and in EU member states where the worker carries out activity for a period not exceeding 15 days, and for longer periods or for activity in non-EU states an extension of cover must be contracted.

briefs.notObvious: The limit is per stay rather than per year, and the cover simply runs out mid-assignment instead of failing at the border.

source.authority: Autoridade de Supervisão de Seguros e Fundos de Pensões

briefs.title: Forty hours of training a year, and what unused hours turn into
briefs.userQuestion: My employer never gave me any training. Does that matter?
briefs.scenario: A worker treats missed training as the employer's oversight rather than an entitlement accumulating in their name.
briefs.audience: employees on permanent contracts
briefs.promise: The annual training minimum, what happens to hours the employer does not deliver, and the notice needed to spend them yourself.

anchorFact.claim: The law establishes a right to a minimum of 40 hours of annual formação contínua for indefinite-term employment contracts, and hours the employer does not provide are converted into an equal number of training hour credits usable on the worker's own initiative with at least 10 days' notice to the employer, expiring 3 years after they were created.

briefs.notObvious: The hours do not simply disappear. They become a balance with a three-year expiry that the worker, not the employer, decides how to spend.

source.authority: Diário da República / Código do Trabalho

briefs.title: The training hours an employer pays for on the way out
briefs.userQuestion: Is there anything owed to me at the end of a contract besides holiday pay?
briefs.scenario: A worker signs off on a final settlement that quietly omits years of undelivered training.
briefs.audience: employees whose contract is ending
briefs.promise: Why undelivered training becomes money at termination, and the official simulator that puts a figure on it.

anchorFact.claim: Training hours not provided by the employer are converted into training hour credits that confer on the worker the right to the corresponding remuneration, and the Autoridade para as Condições do Trabalho publishes a simulator to calculate the amounts due under the right to formação contínua when a contract terminates.

briefs.notObvious: There is a public calculator for this, which means the amount is checkable before signing anything rather than argued about afterwards.

source.authority: Diário da República / Código do Trabalho

briefs.title: Twenty days of employer silence grants the flexible schedule
briefs.userQuestion: My employer never answered my request for flexible hours. What now?
briefs.scenario: A parent whose request went unanswered assumes it was ignored and keeps working the old schedule.
briefs.audience: parents of children under 12
briefs.promise: The narrow grounds for refusal, the twenty-day clock, and what an employer's silence legally amounts to.

anchorFact.claim: An employer may refuse horário flexível for a worker with a child under 12 only on grounds of imperious operating requirements or the impossibility of replacing an indispensable worker, must communicate an intention to refuse within 20 days of receiving the request, and a failure to communicate within that period or to submit the process in the legal term implies acceptance of the request in the exact terms in which it was made.

briefs.notObvious: Silence is not a refusal, it is an approval, and it approves the schedule exactly as the parent wrote it.

briefs.title: A home in Portugal can make you tax resident without the days
briefs.userQuestion: How many days in Portugal make me resident for tax?
briefs.scenario: Someone counts days carefully to stay under the limit while keeping a home here, and is treated as resident anyway.
briefs.audience: people splitting time between countries
briefs.promise: The two independent residency tests, the reporting window once either is met, and the penalty for an out-of-date address.

anchorFact.claim: Under artigo 16 of the Código do IRS a person is resident where they remain more than 183 days, consecutive or interpolated, in any 12-month period beginning or ending in the year in question, or where they hold a habitation in conditions suggesting a current intention to keep and occupy it as habitual residence; once either is verified the residence must be reported within 60 days, and an out-of-date tax address can carry fines up to 375 euros.

briefs.notObvious: The two tests are alternatives rather than a combined score, so keeping a home here can settle the question no matter how the days fall.

briefs.title: The European card gives you local treatment, not free treatment
briefs.userQuestion: Does the European health card cover everything if I fall ill abroad?
briefs.scenario: A traveller relies on the card as insurance, receives care in a country with high user charges, and is billed.
briefs.audience: people travelling in Europe
briefs.promise: What the card actually entitles you to, the countries it reaches, and the substitute document when it cannot arrive in time.

anchorFact.claim: The Cartão Europeu de Seguro de Doença gives care on the same terms as beneficiaries of the social security system of the country you are in, which means care may not be free and taxas moderadoras or co-payments may apply; it is valid in European Union member states, Liechtenstein, Norway, Iceland, Switzerland and the United Kingdom, and the Certificado Provisório de Substituição has the same legal value with a validity of 3 months.
anchorFact.namedThing: Cartão Europeu de Seguro de Doença

briefs.notObvious: It equalises you with a local, and a local pays what locals pay. In some countries that is far more than nothing.

briefs.title: Thirty days to renew a card that takes a week to arrive
briefs.userQuestion: When should I renew the European health card before a trip?
briefs.scenario: Someone requests the card days before travelling and leaves without it, or renews too early and is refused.
briefs.audience: Segurança Social beneficiaries planning travel
briefs.promise: The card's validity, the narrow renewal window, and the delivery time to build into a trip.

anchorFact.claim: The Cartão Europeu de Seguro de Doença is valid for 3 years and renewal must be made in the last 30 days before the validity shown on the card ends; beneficiaries with a NISS request it through Segurança Social Direta and delivery takes 5 to 7 working days, posted to the address registered in the Sistema de Informação da Segurança Social.

briefs.notObvious: It is posted to the address Segurança Social holds, not the one you type into the request, so a stale address quietly loses the card.

briefs.title: The February report that keeps a long lease's tax rate
briefs.userQuestion: Do I have to tell Finanças how long my rental contract runs?
briefs.scenario: A landlord on a long contract never reports its duration and is taxed at the standard rate instead of the reduced one.
briefs.audience: landlords with contracts of two years or more
briefs.promise: Which contracts must be reported, what has to be declared about them, and the February date the report is due.

anchorFact.claim: An owner with arrendamento contracts for long-duration permanent housing, meaning a duration of 2 years or more, must communicate the duration of those contracts and any cessations to the Autoridade Tributária by 15 February, which in 2026 fell on 16 February.

briefs.notObvious: Cessations are reported on the same date as durations, so ending a long lease quietly creates a February obligation of its own.

briefs.title: Three euros a day when your number moves late
briefs.userQuestion: My number did not transfer on the agreed day. Is the operator liable?
briefs.scenario: A customer waits days for a number to move, complains, and is offered goodwill instead of the compensation the rules already require.
briefs.audience: people switching telecom operator
briefs.promise: The legal porting deadline, the daily compensation for missing it, and the fact that you do not have to ask for it.

anchorFact.claim: Portabilidade and activation must happen on the date expressly agreed with the new company and within one business day of that date, and where the deadline is missed the new company must compensate the user 3 euros per number for each complete day of delay, credited without any prior request on the next invoice or by direct means within a maximum of 30 days.

briefs.notObvious: No claim is needed. The credit is owed automatically, which means an unpaid one is a billing error you can point at rather than a favour to negotiate.

briefs.title: Twenty-three euros a day if your number is taken without consent
briefs.userQuestion: Another operator ported my number without asking. What am I owed?
briefs.scenario: Someone whose number was moved by a mis-sold or fraudulent request focuses on getting it back and never claims the compensation attached to every day it was gone.
briefs.audience: people whose number was moved without authorisation
briefs.promise: The daily amount owed for an unauthorised port, and the ceiling that applies per request.

anchorFact.claim: Where a number is transferred to another company without the user's consent, the user has the right to compensation of 23 euros per number for each day the number remains improperly ported until the situation is corrected, up to a maximum of 5,750 euros per portability request.

briefs.notObvious: The amount is nearly eight times the ordinary late-porting rate, which is what makes documenting the exact days worth doing.

briefs.title: The thirty days between a missed bill and a dead contract
briefs.userQuestion: How long before my operator cuts me off for an unpaid bill?
briefs.scenario: A customer disputing a charge stops paying, hears nothing useful, and finds the contract terminated rather than paused.
briefs.audience: customers behind on a telecom bill
briefs.promise: The written warning the operator owes you, the extra time it grants, the three ways to use that time, and when the contract ends by itself.

anchorFact.claim: An electronic communications company must send a written pré-aviso within 10 days of a bill's due date granting a further 30 days to pay before the service is suspended, during which the consumer may pay, agree a written payment plan or dispute the amounts in writing; on payment or a written agreement the service must be restored immediately or within 5 working days where that is not technically possible, and after 30 days of suspension without payment or agreement the contract is automatically terminated.

briefs.notObvious: Disputing the amount in writing counts as using the thirty days. Disputing it by phone does not, and the clock runs either way.

briefs.title: The days of the week the power cannot be cut off
briefs.userQuestion: Can my supplier cut the electricity whenever it wants?
briefs.scenario: A household expecting to be cut off before a long weekend panics, or is cut off on a day the rules do not allow and never challenges it.
briefs.audience: domestic electricity customers behind on a bill
briefs.promise: The written notice required before a cut, the longer notice for social tariff customers, and the days a cut may not happen on.

anchorFact.claim: Before interrupting supply the electricity supplier must send written notice 20 days in advance, extended to 20 business days for customers on the social tariff, stating the causes of the cut, how it can be avoided and the costs of the cut and of restoring supply; for customers on normal low voltage, including domestic consumers, the cut may not take place on Fridays, on the eve of holidays, on holidays or at weekends.

briefs.notObvious: The banned days exist so nobody is left without power over a weekend with no one to call, which also means a cut on one of them is challengeable.

briefs.title: The step down to 1.15 kVA before the supply ends
briefs.userQuestion: Is there anything between missing a payment and losing the electricity?
briefs.scenario: A household sees the power weaken, assumes a fault, and misses the twenty days it has left before supply stops.
briefs.audience: domestic electricity customers in arrears
briefs.promise: The reduction stage that comes before disconnection, the notice it requires, and the clock it starts.

anchorFact.claim: For electricity customers in normal low voltage, and where there is access to the installation, supply may only be interrupted for non-payment after the contracted power has been reduced to 1.15 kVA; the reduction must be communicated in writing with at least 5 days' notice, and interruption may then follow 20 days from the date of the reduction.

briefs.notObvious: The weak supply is the warning, not a fault. It is a twenty-day window that most households spend calling the electrician instead of the supplier.

briefs.title: The twenty-four hours before a job starts
briefs.userQuestion: When is my employer supposed to register me with Segurança Social?
briefs.scenario: A new hire starts work on a promise that the paperwork will follow, and has no contribution record for the months it takes.
briefs.audience: people starting a new job
briefs.promise: When the employer must declare the hire, how the penalty escalates with delay, and the point at which it stops being a fine.

anchorFact.claim: An employer must communicate a worker's admission to Segurança Social in the 24 hours preceding the start of the employment contract's effects; failing to do so is a light contraordenação where the duty is met within the 24 hours following the deadline and a serious contraordenação otherwise, and an employer who has not communicated the admission within 6 months of the legal deadline may be punished with imprisonment up to 3 years or a fine up to 360 days.

briefs.notObvious: The obligation runs before the first day, not after it, so a worker who has already started and is still unregistered is past the deadline rather than inside a grace period.

briefs.title: The declaration the worker owes, not just the employer
briefs.userQuestion: Do I have to tell Segurança Social about a new job myself?
briefs.scenario: A worker assumes registration is entirely the employer's job and never checks, so nothing is declared by either side.
briefs.audience: workers starting with a new employer
briefs.promise: The worker's own twenty-four-hour obligation, and how the NISS is assigned when a foreign worker has none.

anchorFact.claim: A worker must declare to the social security institution for the area of the workplace the start of activity or the link to a new employer within 24 hours after the employment contract takes effect, and where a person has no NISS the employer must first establish the contract and communicate the employment relationship in Segurança Social Direta so the number can be assigned.

briefs.notObvious: Both sides have a twenty-four-hour duty pointing in opposite directions: the employer's runs before the contract takes effect, the worker's after.

briefs.title: A reunification decision expires if the visa is not requested
briefs.userQuestion: We were granted family reunification. Is there another deadline?
briefs.scenario: A family celebrates the recognition, waits for documents to be legalised abroad, and lets the decision lapse before the visa is applied for.
briefs.audience: families reuniting from outside Portugal
briefs.promise: The second deadline after the right is recognised, and what missing it does to the decision already granted.

anchorFact.claim: Where the family member is outside Portugal the residence visa for reagrupamento familiar must be applied for within 90 days, and failure to apply for the residence visa within that period causes the decision recognising the right to family reunification to lapse.

briefs.notObvious: Winning the right is not the last step. It has its own expiry, and it runs while the family is still gathering documents abroad.

briefs.title: Ten days to cancel a citizen card you cannot find
briefs.userQuestion: I lost my Cartão de Cidadão. What do I have to do, and by when?
briefs.scenario: Someone searches the house for a fortnight before reporting the loss, leaving the card usable and the deadline missed.
briefs.audience: people who lost or had a citizen card stolen
briefs.promise: The deadline to cancel, the free 24-hour route to do it, the fact that cancelling is final, and what a replacement costs.
