anchorFact.claim: A Cartão de Cidadão that is lost, destroyed or stolen must be cancelled within 10 days of learning what happened to it; cancellation is free and can be done online or by phone through the Linha Cartão de Cidadão on 210 990 111, which operates 24 hours a day 7 days a week; a cancelled card can never be reactivated, and an online replacement request for a card with validity up to 5 years costs 13.50 euros.

briefs.notObvious: Cancellation is irreversible, which is why people delay it. The ten days run from when you realised, not from when you give up looking.

source.authority: gov.pt / Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado

briefs.title: Twelve months to claim the car tax exemption for moving here
briefs.userQuestion: Can I bring my car when I move to Portugal without paying ISV?
briefs.scenario: Someone moves, settles in, deals with the car a year and a half later, and pays full ISV on a vehicle that would have come in free.
briefs.audience: people moving to Portugal with a vehicle
briefs.promise: The exemption for transferring residence, the twelve-month deadline, the one-vehicle limit, and the only channel that accepts the request.

anchorFact.claim: A person transferring their legal residence from another Member State or a third country to Portugal may request ISV exemption for a vehicle brought with them up to 12 months from the date of the residence transfer, each person may request the exemption for only 1 vehicle, and requests are submitted exclusively through the Portal das Finanças by electronic transmission of the Declaração Aduaneira de Veículo.

briefs.notObvious: The clock starts at the residence transfer, not at the car's arrival, so a vehicle shipped late can be inside its own deadlines and outside this one.

briefs.title: The hundred euros of car tax a clean engine cannot avoid
briefs.userQuestion: Can a low-emission car end up with no ISV at all?
briefs.scenario: An importer of a low-emission vehicle calculates a negative environmental component and budgets for zero tax.
briefs.audience: people importing a low-emission vehicle
briefs.promise: How the two ISV components interact when one is negative, and the floor the total cannot go below.

anchorFact.claim: ISV on passenger vehicles combines a cilindrada component and an environmental component from Tabela A, and where the environmental component produces a negative value it is deducted from the cilindrada component, with the total tax payable never being less than 100 euros.

briefs.notObvious: A negative environmental component is a discount on the other half of the bill, not a refund, and the floor stops it reaching zero.

briefs.title: The procedure your bank must open when you fall behind
briefs.userQuestion: I have missed loan payments. Does the bank have to do anything before acting?
briefs.scenario: A borrower in arrears waits for a demand letter, not knowing a formal procedure with its own deadline should already be running.
briefs.audience: borrowers who have missed a loan payment
briefs.promise: The extrajudicial procedure that opens on default, the deadline for the bank's proposals, and the two things it may not charge you for.

anchorFact.claim: Under the general regime of the Decreto-Lei n.º 227/2012 the credit institution must present the customer with one or more proposals to regularise the default within 30 days of the start of PERSI, and it may not charge commissions or increase the interest rate of the credit contract as a result of renegotiating the contract conditions within PERSI.

briefs.notObvious: Renegotiating inside the procedure is protected from repricing, which makes the moment the bank opens it worth knowing and asking about.

briefs.title: The plan that starts before a payment is missed
briefs.userQuestion: I am about to struggle with repayments. Is it too early to talk to the bank?
briefs.scenario: A borrower whose income has dropped waits to actually default before contacting the bank, losing the stage designed to prevent it.
briefs.audience: borrowers whose income has fallen
briefs.promise: The risk signals banks must monitor, the fifteen days they then have to propose something, and the repricing they are barred from.

anchorFact.claim: Under PARI institutions must regularly assess credit contracts for signs of deteriorating borrower financial capacity, with unemployment, loss of borrower income and working in a sector in difficulty counting as default risk indicators, and where the risk is confirmed and the customer has financial capacity the institution must present adequate proposals within 15 days of receiving the information and documents it requested; institutions are prohibited from increasing the contractually agreed interest rate in proposals presented under PARI or PERSI.

briefs.notObvious: Losing income is itself a listed trigger, so reporting it early puts the bank on a fifteen-day clock rather than putting you on a watchlist.

briefs.title: Paying IVA when the client pays, and the month to ask
briefs.userQuestion: Can I stop paying IVA on invoices my clients have not settled?
briefs.scenario: A business carrying IVA on unpaid invoices decides in March to change regime and finds the door does not open until October.
briefs.audience: businesses waiting on late-paying clients
briefs.promise: The turnover limit for cash accounting, the single month the option can be exercised, when it takes effect, and the waits that apply to rejoining.

anchorFact.claim: The regime de IVA de caixa requires previous-year turnover of 2,000,000 euros or less, the option may be exercised only during the month of October each year and takes effect on 1 January of the following year, the request is validated rather than granted automatically, and rejoining requires that a previous option ended at least 2 consecutive calendar years earlier, or that 1 year has passed since regularising a tax situation where the regime was terminated for irregularity; leaving for the general exigibility regime is only possible after 2 consecutive calendar years under the cash regime.

briefs.notObvious: One month a year, effective the following January. Deciding in the month the cash-flow problem bites is already too late by up to eleven months.

briefs.title: The rent-to-value ratio that lets a landlord charge IVA
briefs.userQuestion: Can I charge IVA on a commercial letting and deduct what I spend?
briefs.scenario: A landlord refurbishing a unit for a business tenant absorbs the IVA on the works, not knowing the exemption can be waived.
briefs.audience: landlords letting to businesses
briefs.promise: What waiving the IVA exemption unlocks, the certificate it requires, and the two conditions including the rent ratio.

anchorFact.claim: Under the Decreto-Lei n.º 21/2007 a taxable person wishing to waive the IVA exemption on immovable property must ask the Autoridade Tributária for a certificado de renúncia; the waiver is admissible where the property is used for activities giving a right to deduct IVA and, in the case of letting, where the annual rent is equal to or greater than 25ths of the property's acquisition or construction value, and those who waive gain the right to deduct the tax borne on that property.

briefs.notObvious: The rent has to clear a fraction of what the property cost, so a below-market rent to a friendly tenant can quietly disqualify the deduction on the works.

briefs.title: Using another country's digital ID to log in here
briefs.userQuestion: Can I access Portuguese public services before I have a Chave Móvel Digital?
briefs.scenario: A newly arrived EU citizen waits weeks for a Portuguese credential while holding a national eID that already works.
briefs.audience: EU citizens new to Portugal
briefs.promise: The European authentication route into Portuguese public services, and the date from which it has been available.

anchorFact.claim: Under the eIDAS interoperability platform, since 29 September 2018 an EU citizen holding a notified national eID can access any public service online in any Member State, and Autenticação Europeia lets citizens of participating Member States confirm their identity to reach online services provided by Portuguese public entities.

briefs.notObvious: The credential you already own may be accepted here on day one, which removes the usual wait before anything official can be done online.

briefs.title: Free school books are lent, and damage is billed
briefs.userQuestion: Do we keep the free textbooks at the end of the year?
briefs.scenario: A family lets a child write in and dog-ear books that must be handed back, and is charged for them in July.
briefs.audience: parents using free textbooks
briefs.promise: When the books have to go back, how their condition is treated, and who pays when it is poor.

anchorFact.claim: Textbooks distributed free of charge must be returned at the end of each school year, or at the end of the study cycle for subjects with final exams; their condition is assessed on return and where a textbook is in poor condition the encarregado de educação must cover its cost.

briefs.notObvious: Subjects with final exams keep their books to the end of the cycle while everything else goes back yearly, so the return date is not the same for every book in the bag.

briefs.title: Only the registered guardian can pull the textbook vouchers
briefs.userQuestion: Who requests the free textbook vouchers, and where do they appear?
briefs.scenario: A student or a grandparent tries to collect the books and finds the vouchers cannot be issued to them.
briefs.audience: families of school-age children
briefs.promise: Where the vouchers live, who is allowed to request them, and how release is staggered across year groups.

anchorFact.claim: Vouchers for free textbooks are issued in the name of students in compulsory education from the 1st to the 12th year at public schools and private schools with association contracts, but may only be requested by the encarregado de educação through the MEGA platform or the Edu Rede Escolar app, which also lists the bookshops where the books can be collected, and release is staggered by year group across late July and August.

briefs.notObvious: The voucher belongs to the child but only one registered adult can release it, which is what strands families where that adult is unavailable in August.

briefs.title: The child top-up nobody has to apply for
briefs.userQuestion: Is there anything beyond abono de família for a low-income household?
briefs.scenario: A family already receiving family allowance never learns a second payment exists, or waits for a form that does not exist.
briefs.audience: low-income households receiving family allowance
briefs.promise: The three cumulative conditions for the child guarantee, the income formula behind them, and why no application is needed.

anchorFact.claim: Entitlement to the garantia para a infância requires cumulatively that the child holds abono de família for crianças e jovens, is under 18, and belongs to a household whose reference income is below 0.35 times the IAS times 14; the amount paid is the difference needed to reach a guaranteed monthly total, it arrives together with the abono de família, and attribution is automatic so the family does not have to request it.

briefs.notObvious: It is a top-up to a guaranteed floor rather than a fixed payment, so the amount falls as the allowance rises and reaching the floor is the point.

source.authority: Garantia para a Infância / Instituto da Segurança Social

briefs.title: Twelve days a year, and the two ceilings on top of it
briefs.userQuestion: How much is redundancy compensation actually worth?
briefs.scenario: A worker multiplies years by a monthly salary, expects a large sum, and is surprised twice by caps nobody mentioned.
briefs.audience: workers facing redundancy
briefs.promise: The days per year of service, the ceiling on the pay used in the calculation, and the ceiling on the total.

anchorFact.claim: A worker dismissed in a despedimento coletivo, and equally in a dismissal for extinction of the post, is entitled to compensation of 12 days of base remuneration and supplements for each complete year of seniority; the base remuneration and supplements taken into account may not exceed 20 times the retribuição mínima mensal garantida, and the total compensation may not exceed 12 times the worker's monthly base remuneration and supplements or, where the previous limit applies, 240 times the RMMG.

briefs.notObvious: There are two separate caps, one on the input and one on the output, so a long career at a good salary is limited twice over rather than once.

briefs.title: Accepting the redundancy money closes the door on contesting it
briefs.userQuestion: Can I take the compensation now and still dispute the dismissal?
briefs.scenario: A worker banks the payment to cover the coming month and finds the legal challenge is no longer available.
briefs.audience: workers who believe their dismissal was unlawful
briefs.promise: Why receiving the compensation forecloses a challenge, and what returning it requires and when.

anchorFact.claim: To challenge a despedimento coletivo, a dismissal for extinction of the post or a dismissal for unsuitability, the worker must not receive the dismissal compensation, and where it has been received it must be returned in full simultaneously with the opposition to the dismissal.

briefs.notObvious: Full return has to happen at the same moment as the challenge, not later, which turns a routine bank transfer into a decision with a deadline.

briefs.title: Three more months per parent, paid at a quarter
briefs.userQuestion: Is there any paid leave left after the initial parental leave ends?
briefs.scenario: A couple treats the end of initial parental leave as the end of paid options and one parent resigns instead.
briefs.audience: parents of children under six
briefs.promise: The length and pay rate of extended parental leave, the age limit it runs to, and the unpaid assistance leave that follows it.

anchorFact.claim: Licença parental alargada for assistance to a child up to 6 years of age lasts up to 3 months paid at 25 per cent of reference remuneration where it is taken immediately after the initial parental benefit or after the other parent's extended benefit; each parent has the right to a full 3 months, which may be taken by both or by one, alternately or at the same time, and once exhausted parents may take child assistance leave up to a limit of 2 years, or 3 years for a third or subsequent child.

briefs.notObvious: Three months belongs to each parent rather than to the couple, and the entitlement stays open until the child turns six rather than expiring with the initial leave.

briefs.title: Six months of contributions before a sick child is covered
briefs.userQuestion: Will I be paid for the days I take off when my child is ill?
briefs.scenario: A recently hired parent takes days off for a sick child and finds nothing is paid because the contribution record is short.
briefs.audience: working parents of a sick child
briefs.promise: The contribution record the benefit needs, whose children count, and the two percentages that set the daily amount.

anchorFact.claim: The subsídio para assistência a filho requires 6 months of work with contributions, consecutive or not, to Segurança Social or another social protection system on the day the leave starts; it covers biological, adopted and spouse's children, adult children who are part of the household, and children of any age with a disability or chronic illness, and the daily amount is 100 per cent of net reference remuneration with a floor of 65 per cent of reference remuneration.

briefs.notObvious: The six months need not be consecutive and may come from another country's system, which quietly qualifies parents who assume a short Portuguese record disqualifies them.

briefs.title: Three refusals and the regulator picks your insurer
briefs.userQuestion: No insurer will cover my car. Can I be left without compulsory insurance?
briefs.scenario: A driver refused by several insurers after a claim history stops driving, or drives uninsured, believing there is no route left.
briefs.audience: drivers refused compulsory motor insurance
briefs.promise: What to collect from each insurer that refuses you, how many refusals it takes, and who then assigns a company obliged to accept.

anchorFact.claim: Insurers may refuse to write compulsory motor insurance, but anyone who fails to obtain acceptance from at least 3 insurers may demand a declaração de recusa from each, which insurers are obliged to provide, and on presenting those documents to the Autoridade de Supervisão de Seguros e Fundos de Pensões the regulator designates which insurer is obliged to accept the policy.

briefs.notObvious: A refusal is not a dead end, it is a document. Three of them turn the regulator into the one who decides who covers you.

source.authority: Autoridade de Supervisão de Seguros e Fundos de Pensões

briefs.title: Thirty days before renewal, in both directions
briefs.userQuestion: My premium went up at renewal. Was I supposed to be told?
briefs.scenario: A driver notices a higher premium after it has already renewed, and has also missed the window to leave.
briefs.audience: motor insurance policyholders
briefs.promise: The notice an insurer owes before changing your premium, and the matching notice you must give to stop the policy renewing.

anchorFact.claim: Before changing the premium the insurer must notify the policyholder at least 30 days before the contract's renewal date, and a policyholder who wants to prevent the contract renewing must denounce it 30 days before the renewal date; premiums rise with claims for which the insured is responsible and fall for each year without claims under bónus and malus.

briefs.notObvious: The two clocks are the same length and run at the same time, so the notice of an increase arrives exactly as your own window to leave closes.

source.authority: Autoridade de Supervisão de Seguros e Fundos de Pensões

briefs.title: The certificate that carries your cover to another insurer
briefs.userQuestion: Can I change health insurer without starting the exclusions again?
briefs.scenario: Someone stays with an expensive insurer for years because switching seems to mean declaring everything afresh and waiting all over again.
briefs.audience: people buying private health insurance
briefs.promise: The standard-conditions regime behind pre-existing cover, and the certificate that lets cover follow you to a new insurer.

anchorFact.claim: The ASF standard conditions regime for doenças preexistentes includes congenital diseases and creates a certificado de pré-existências that allows the choice of another insurer with continuity of cover, a portability subject to defined conditions.

briefs.notObvious: Portability exists as a named document, so the question to ask a new insurer is not whether they will cover the condition but whether they accept the certificate.

source.authority: Autoridade de Supervisão de Seguros e Fundos de Pensões

briefs.title: Accepting an inheritance plainly can cost more than it gives
briefs.userQuestion: Can I inherit debts that are larger than the estate?
briefs.scenario: An heir signs for a modest inheritance without checking the debts and ends up answering for them out of their own assets.
briefs.audience: people named as heirs
briefs.promise: The two protective ways to take an inheritance, the exposure of taking it plainly, and the form a refusal must take.

anchorFact.claim: An heir who suspects an inheritance is in deficit should repudiate it or accept it a benefício de inventário, since otherwise they risk answering with their own assets and beyond the value of the assets received; repúdio is a unilateral formal legal act that must be made by escritura pública where the estate includes immovable property, and the right to accept or repudiate may be exercised within 10 years.

briefs.notObvious: The protection is in how you accept, not whether you accept, and the difference is a single phrase in the document.

briefs.title: The two-thirds of an estate a will cannot touch
briefs.userQuestion: How much of my estate can I actually leave to whoever I want?
briefs.scenario: Someone writes a will leaving everything to one person and creates a dispute the law will resolve against them.
briefs.audience: people making a will
briefs.promise: The protected share when a spouse and children inherit together, what is left freely disposable, and what goes into the calculation.

anchorFact.claim: Where a spouse and children concur, the legítima is two thirds of the inheritance, leaving one third as the quota disponível, and the calculation of both takes into account the value of the assets in the deceased's patrimony at the date of death, the value of donated assets, expenses subject to collation and the debts of the inheritance.

briefs.notObvious: Lifetime gifts are added back before the share is worked out, so giving assets away early does not enlarge the part a will can direct.

briefs.title: Two days to tell your boss, one day for them to tell the insurer
briefs.userQuestion: What has to happen, and how fast, after an accident at work?
briefs.scenario: A worker mentions a minor injury in passing, nothing is filed, and the claim is contested weeks later when it turns out to be serious.
briefs.audience: workers injured on the job
briefs.promise: The worker's reporting window, the employer's separate window to notify the insurer, and the rule for fatal accidents.

anchorFact.claim: After a workplace accident the worker, personally or through someone else, must report it in writing or verbally to their superior within 2 business days, and the employer as policyholder must notify the insurer within 24 hours of learning of the accident, reporting fatal accidents to the insurer immediately.

briefs.notObvious: Two separate clocks run from two different events, so a worker who reported on time can still be left uncovered by an employer who did not.

source.authority: Autoridade para as Condições do Trabalho

briefs.title: The prosecutor who represents injured workers for free
briefs.userQuestion: The insurer says it was not a work accident. Do I need to hire a lawyer?
briefs.scenario: A worker whose accident is disputed drops the claim on the assumption that fighting an insurer means legal fees they cannot afford.
briefs.audience: workers whose accident claim is disputed
briefs.promise: Who defends and represents work accident victims, which court it sits in, and how to reach it.

anchorFact.claim: Where there is a dispute about whether an event constitutes an acidente de trabalho, the injured worker should contact the Ministério Público of the labour court for their area of residence, which is the entity responsible for defending and representing victims of work accidents.

briefs.notObvious: Representation in these cases is a public function rather than a service you buy, which changes the calculation for anyone who assumed the insurer had the deeper pockets.

source.authority: Autoridade de Supervisão de Seguros e Fundos de Pensões

briefs.title: One year to claim the wages an insolvent employer never paid
briefs.userQuestion: My employer went under owing me pay. Is that money simply lost?
briefs.scenario: A worker joins the insolvency queue, hears nothing for eighteen months, and misses the separate fund that would have paid part of it.
briefs.audience: workers owed pay by a failing employer
briefs.promise: The three situations that open the fund, the one-year claim window, and the monthly and overall caps on what it pays.

anchorFact.claim: The Fundo de Garantia Salarial covers employer debts to employees where there is an insolvency judgment, a court order appointing a provisional judicial administrator in a Processo Especial de Revitalização, or acceptance of a company recovery request by IAPMEI; the claim must be submitted to Segurança Social within 1 year from the day following contract termination, and the fund pays a maximum of 6 months' pay with a monthly ceiling of 3 times the minimum wage.

briefs.notObvious: The year runs from the end of the contract, not from the insolvency ruling, so waiting for the court to finish is how the window is usually missed.

briefs.title: The guarantee that expires if the decision takes too long
briefs.userQuestion: I posted a guarantee to pause a tax execution. Does it just sit there?
briefs.scenario: A taxpayer ties up money or a bank guarantee for years without realising it should have lapsed once the deadlines passed.
briefs.audience: taxpayers contesting a tax debt
briefs.promise: What suspends a tax execution, and the two waiting periods after which the guarantee lapses by itself.

anchorFact.claim: A tax execution is suspended where an adequate guarantee and a request are presented together stating the nature of the debt, the period concerned, the entity that issued the act and the intention to challenge; the garantia expires automatically if the reclamação graciosa is not decided within 1 year, or if no first-instance decision is issued in the impugnação judicial or opposition within 4 years.

briefs.notObvious: Expiry is automatic on the calendar rather than on request, so a guarantee still in place after those periods is one nobody has released.

briefs.title: Two thirds of net pay is out of reach of a seizure
briefs.userQuestion: How much of my salary can actually be taken for a debt?
briefs.scenario: Someone facing enforcement expects to lose their whole wage and makes decisions, or hides income, on that assumption.
briefs.audience: people facing enforcement over a debt
briefs.promise: The protected share of wages and periodic payments, and the fraction a seizure can actually reach.

anchorFact.claim: Under artigo 738 of the Código de Processo Civil two thirds of the net part of wages, salaries and periodic payments are not susceptible to seizure, so a penhora may reach only 1 third of the net amount.

briefs.notObvious: The protection is on the net figure and applies to periodic payments generally, not only to an employment salary.

source.authority: Diário da República / Código de Processo Civil

briefs.title: Eight years before a tax debt prescribes, and where the count starts
briefs.userQuestion: Does an old tax debt ever go away?
briefs.scenario: Someone assumes an old assessment is dead, or conversely that it is eternal, and never checks which year the clock started in.
briefs.audience: people carrying an old tax debt
briefs.promise: The prescription period for tax debts and the two different starting points depending on the kind of tax.

anchorFact.claim: Under artigo 48 of the Lei Geral Tributária tax debts prescribe after 8 years, counted for periodic taxes from the end of the year in which the taxable event occurred, and for taxes of a single obligation from the date the taxable event occurred.

briefs.notObvious: For a periodic tax the count starts at the end of the year rather than at the assessment, which can move the date by well over a year in either direction.

source.authority: Diário da República / Lei Geral Tributária

briefs.title: Five years on a Segurança Social debt, and what restarts it
briefs.userQuestion: How long can Segurança Social pursue unpaid contributions?
briefs.scenario: Someone counts five quiet years and assumes an old contribution debt is gone, without accounting for the letters that reset the clock.
briefs.audience: people with unpaid Segurança Social contributions
briefs.promise: The prescription period for contributions and quotizações, where it starts, and the kind of step that interrupts it.

anchorFact.claim: Under the Código dos Regimes Contributivos the obligation to pay quotizações and contribuições prescribes after 5 years counted from the date the obligation should have been met, and prescription is interrupted by any administrative step aimed at assessing or collecting the debt that is carried out with the knowledge of the person responsible for payment.

briefs.notObvious: Any collection step you were told about restarts the five years, so the quiet period has to be quiet from their side, not just from yours.

source.authority: Diário da República / Código dos Regimes Contributivos

briefs.title: Two funeral payments, six months apart in their deadlines
briefs.userQuestion: Can I get help with funeral costs I paid for?
briefs.scenario: Someone who paid for a funeral applies under the wrong scheme months later and finds the ninety-day one has closed.
briefs.audience: people who paid for a funeral
briefs.promise: The two separate schemes, who each is for, the very different windows, and the ceiling on what is paid.

anchorFact.claim: The subsídio de funeral can be requested up to 6 months after the first day of the month following the death and pays a maximum of 3 times the IAS, published as 1,611.39 euros, while the separate reembolso de despesas de funeral must be requested within 90 consecutive days of the date of death by someone who paid for the funeral of a beneficiary of the general Segurança Social regime where the costs were not borne by the person entitled to the subsídio por morte.

briefs.notObvious: Which scheme applies depends on the dead person's cover, not on who paid, and picking the wrong one can burn the shorter of two very different deadlines.

briefs.title: Why one parcel clears customs and the next one waits
briefs.userQuestion: Why did I have to pay extra on a parcel from outside the EU?
briefs.scenario: A shopper orders two similar items from abroad, one arrives normally and the other is held with fees to pay, with no obvious difference between them.
briefs.audience: people ordering from outside the EU
briefs.promise: The value line under which a parcel need not stop, what the seller has to have done, and the separate fee the carrier can add.

anchorFact.claim: For postal items valued up to 150 euros, where the seller includes IVA in the final price the parcel does not have to stop at the border for IVA payment; postal items from outside the EU customs territory are presented to customs by CTT, which submits an electronic import declaration based on information given through the clearance portal, and CTT or the carrier may also charge a clearance fee on top of the tax.

briefs.notObvious: What decides it is whether the seller collected the IVA at checkout, not the value alone, which is why two parcels of the same price behave differently.

briefs.title: Twelve years and 135 centimetres, and both have to be true
briefs.userQuestion: When can my child stop using a car seat?
briefs.scenario: A tall ten-year-old is moved out of a restraint, or a short teenager is kept in one, because only one of the two tests is remembered.
briefs.audience: parents driving children
briefs.promise: The two conditions that decide whether a restraint is required, where the child must sit, and the transport types exempted.

anchorFact.claim: Children under 12 years of age and less than 135 cm tall must be carried in the rear seat of vehicles fitted with seat belts using a homologated sistema de retenção adapted to their weight and height, while public passenger transport, TVDE and patient transport vehicles are exempt provided the child travels in the rear.

briefs.notObvious: Both conditions have to hold for the requirement to apply, so a child who clears either the age or the height leaves the rule behind.

source.authority: Diário da República / Código da Estrada

briefs.title: The two degrees of dependency, and what separates them
briefs.userQuestion: My parent needs daily help. Is there a pension top-up for that?
briefs.scenario: A family caring for a pensioner who cannot wash or move unaided never applies, or applies under the wrong degree.
briefs.audience: families caring for a dependent pensioner
briefs.promise: What each degree of dependency means in practice, and who beyond pensioners can claim the supplement.

anchorFact.claim: The complemento por dependência is paid monthly to pensioners who need another person's help with basic daily needs, at 2 degrees: the 1st covers people who cannot autonomously perform acts indispensable to basic daily needs such as feeding, moving about or personal hygiene, and the 2nd covers people who meet those conditions and are also bedridden or have severe dementia; beneficiaries of the prestação social para a inclusão and non-pensioner beneficiaries with an illness capable of causing special invalidity may also claim.

briefs.notObvious: The second degree is not simply worse than the first, it is the first plus a named condition, so the assessment turns on being bedridden or on a dementia diagnosis.

briefs.title: One certificate that reaches four different taxes
briefs.userQuestion: What do I actually get from a recognised disability, tax-wise?
briefs.scenario: Someone holding a multi-use certificate uses it for social benefits and never registers it with Finanças, missing years of deductions.
briefs.audience: people with a recognised degree of incapacity
briefs.promise: The incapacity level that counts as fiscally relevant, the taxes it reaches, the two IRS deductions, and the fifteen days after registering the claim.

anchorFact.claim: Deficiência fiscalmente relevante is recognised at a grau de incapacidade of 60 per cent or more proven by an atestado médico de incapacidade multiuso and brings benefits under IRS, IUC, ISV and IVA; the request is registered on the Portal das Finanças under Dados Pessoais and the documentation with an authenticated copy of the certificate must be sent within 15 days, and the IRS deduction from the collection is 4 times the IAS for each taxpayer with a disability and 2.5 times the IAS for each dependent or ascendant with one.

briefs.notObvious: The certificate does nothing for tax until it is separately registered with Finanças, and that registration has its own fifteen-day document deadline.

briefs.title: A multi-use certificate does not lapse while you wait
briefs.userQuestion: My incapacity certificate has expired and the medical board has not called me. Do I lose the benefits?
briefs.scenario: Someone whose certificate passed its date stops claiming benefits, or is refused them, while a reassessment appointment is outstanding.
briefs.audience: people holding an incapacity certificate
briefs.promise: What happens to the certificate's validity between its expiry and a new assessment, and what that protects.

anchorFact.claim: Under the rules in force an atestado médico de incapacidade multiuso remains valid until a new evaluation is guaranteed, ensuring the attribution and maintenance of the social, economic and tax benefits recognised for citizens with disabilities.

briefs.notObvious: The waiting time for a junta médica is the State's delay, not yours, and the rule says so explicitly.

briefs.title: What a condominium can and cannot do about a short-let flat
briefs.userQuestion: Can the neighbours have a local lodging registration cancelled?
briefs.scenario: A condominium votes to shut down a short-let flat and assumes the vote itself ends the registration, or an operator assumes a vote is harmless.
briefs.audience: condominium owners and local lodging operators
briefs.promise: The majority a condominium needs, what its deliberation must be based on, and who actually decides on cancellation.

anchorFact.claim: A condominium assembly can no longer cancel an alojamento local registration directly, but may oppose the activity by a justified deliberation approved by more than half of the building's permilagem, based on proven repeated acts that disturb the normal use of the property or cause discomfort affecting residents' rest; the condominium must then request a cancellation decision from the president of the territorially competent câmara municipal, who may invite the parties to reach agreement with or without the assistance of a provedor do alojamento local.

briefs.notObvious: The vote is the start of a municipal procedure, not the end of the business, and it has to rest on documented repeated disturbance rather than on disapproval.

briefs.title: Two years' notice and a year's rent to take a flat back
briefs.userQuestion: My landlord says they need the flat for themselves. How much notice is that?
briefs.scenario: A tenant told to leave in a few months accepts it, not knowing the notice for this ground is measured in years and comes with a payment.
briefs.audience: tenants asked to leave for the owner's own use
briefs.promise: The notice period for this ground, the ownership conditions the landlord must meet, and the indemnity owed to the tenant.

anchorFact.claim: A landlord ending a lease for their own housing must give the tenant notice of not less than 2 years before the intended date of cessation, must have been owner, co-owner or usufructuary of the building for more than 2 years or have acquired it by succession, must not for more than 1 year have owned a house meeting their own or their first-degree descendants' housing needs in the relevant council area, and must pay the tenant an indemnity equal to 1 year of rent.

briefs.notObvious: Every condition is checkable from public records, and a landlord who bought recently or already owns a suitable home cannot use this ground at all.

briefs.title: A rent rise that arrives with less than thirty days' notice
briefs.userQuestion: Can my landlord raise the rent whenever they decide to?
briefs.scenario: A tenant receives a new rent figure days before it applies and pays it, assuming annual increases work that way.
briefs.audience: tenants on an ongoing lease
briefs.promise: Where the annual increase figure comes from, when it is published, and the written notice a landlord must give before applying it.

anchorFact.claim: Rent is updated annually by applying the coeficiente de atualização set for that year under artigo 24 of Lei 6/2006, which the INE must determine and have published by notice in the Diário da República by 30 October, and the landlord must communicate the coefficient and the resulting new rent in writing with a minimum of 30 days' notice.

briefs.notObvious: The figure is published nationally before any landlord applies it, so a tenant can check the lawful increase before the letter arrives.

briefs.title: Four days between the university result and the enrolment deadline
briefs.userQuestion: What happens straight after the first-phase results come out?
briefs.scenario: A family goes away in late August, sees the placement result, and returns to find the enrolment window already shut.
briefs.audience: families of applicants to public higher education
briefs.promise: The three phases of the national competition, the 2026 dates for each, and the short enrolment window that follows the first result.

anchorFact.claim: The concurso nacional de acesso runs in 3 phases: in 2026 the 1st phase application ran from 20 July to 6 August, the 2nd from 25 August to 3 September and the 3rd from 23 to 25 September; 1st phase results were released on 23 August and enrolment at the institution for candidates placed in the 1st phase ran from 24 to 27 August.

briefs.notObvious: The second phase opens two days after the first-phase results, so the decision to accept a placement and the decision to try again are made in the same week.

briefs.title: Travelling abroad with one parent needs no letter
briefs.userQuestion: Do I need the other parent's written permission to take our child abroad?
briefs.scenario: A separated parent cancels a trip, or pays a notary, over a document the law does not require in their situation.
briefs.audience: parents travelling abroad with a child
briefs.promise: The situation that actually triggers the authorisation requirement, the form it must take, and how long a consular one lasts.

anchorFact.claim: Where a minor travels with only one parent, including where the parents are unmarried, divorced, judicially separated or the marriage was annulled, no authorisation is required provided responsabilidade parental is exercised jointly and the other parent does not object; authorisation is required where the minor leaves the country unaccompanied by both parents, must be in a written and dated document with the signature of the holder of parental responsibility legally certified by a notary, lawyer, solicitador or a Portuguese embassy or consulate, granting accompanying powers to identified third parties, and a consular authorisation is valid for 1 year.

briefs.notObvious: The trigger is travelling without both parents, not travelling without one, so the common single-parent holiday needs nothing unless the other parent has formally objected.

briefs.title: The hour of day that decides how fast a passport arrives
briefs.userQuestion: How quickly can I actually get a Portuguese passport?
briefs.scenario: Someone books travel assuming the fastest passport service, then applies in the afternoon and loses a day they had counted on.
briefs.audience: people applying for a Portuguese passport
briefs.promise: The four delivery speeds, the cut-off times that unlock the quickest ones, and the validity for adults and small children.

anchorFact.claim: A Portuguese electronic passport is valid for 5 years, or 2 years for minors under 4; delivery is 5 working days for the standard request, 2 working days where the request is made by 17h, and 1 working day where it is made by 11h, and a request made by 11h under the urgent airport service is delivered the same day from 17h15 at Lisbon airport.

briefs.notObvious: The faster tiers are gated by a clock rather than a fee alone, so the same money bought after 11h buys a slower passport.

source.authority: gov.pt / Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado

briefs.title: An international permit is useless on its own
briefs.userQuestion: Do I need an international driving licence, and what does it actually do?
briefs.scenario: A traveller leaves the Portuguese licence at home with the international permit in their wallet and cannot legally drive or collect a hire car.
briefs.audience: people driving outside Europe
briefs.promise: Where the permit is needed, how long it lasts, what it costs, and the document that must always travel with it.

anchorFact.claim: The licença internacional de condução allows driving outside the EU and EEA in countries that signed the international road traffic conventions and is often required for hire cars; it is valid for 1 year from issue, or for the shorter remaining validity of the underlying licence, costs 30 euros, can only be requested at an IMT counter where it is issued on the spot, and is only valid when presented together with the national licence that supports it.

briefs.notObvious: It is a translation of your licence rather than a licence, which is why it expires with the original and is worthless without it in your pocket.

source.authority: Instituto da Mobilidade e dos Transportes

briefs.title: The published ceiling above which a loan rate is usury
briefs.userQuestion: Is there a legal limit on what a consumer loan can charge me?
briefs.scenario: Someone offered expensive credit assumes the price is simply the market and never checks it against the published ceiling for that credit type.
briefs.audience: people taking out consumer credit
briefs.promise: How the maximum rates are calculated each quarter, the two limits that bind them, and the point at which a rate becomes usurious.

anchorFact.claim: Under the Decreto-Lei n.º 133/2009 the Banco de Portugal determines and publishes quarterly the maximum TAEG for each type of consumer credit, set at the average TAEG charged in the market in the previous quarter increased by one quarter, and these maxima may not exceed the average TAEG of all consumer credit contracts increased by 50 per cent; the maximum TAEG is the limit above which rates are considered usury, and a maximum TAN is also published for the overdraft category.

briefs.notObvious: The ceiling is set per credit type and moves every quarter, so the same rate can be lawful on a car loan and usurious on a personal one.
